book.dracora.guide.page1:
Dragons are rare. Each nest holds a single egg, watched over by its parent.

The parent is shy and gentle. It never fights; a sudden rush only sends it into the sky.
book.dracora.guide.page2:
Earning trust

Come quietly. Sneak close and stay near the nest for half a minute, and the parent shows you hearts.

One visit a day. After three days of calm visits, it trusts you with its egg.
book.dracora.guide.page3:
Taking the egg

With its trust earned, the egg is yours to take: mine it gently.

The parent then flies off to find a new home far away.
book.dracora.guide.page4:
Hatching

Set the egg down beside a lit campfire or lava. With a day of warmth it cracks twice, then hatches.

The little one belongs to whoever set the egg down, even if they're away when it hatches.
book.dracora.guide.page5:
Growing up

A hatchling follows you, and sits or stands when you use an empty hand on it.

After a day it's a juvenile, ready to carry you for short hops. A day later it's grown.
book.dracora.guide.page6:
Flying

Climb on a grown dragon with an empty hand. Hold jump to take off, and look where you want to go.

Let go and it hovers. Step off in the air and it glides down safely.
book.dracora.guide.page7:
Colours

Every dragon wears the colours of the place it was born: snow, jungle, forest, sea, badlands, plains, or the End's own violets.
book.dracora.guide.page8:
Breeding

Two grown dragons of yours, each given raw salmon or cod, lay an egg in a blend of their colours. Once in a while it's a rare pearl or obsidian.

After laying, they rest for a day.
book.dracora.guide.page9:
A dragon is only ever yours when you hatch it: no wild one can be tamed.

Each dragon is one of a kind, and a lost dragon is gone for good. Keep yours close.
